description:
What the OWOX Data Marts LinkedIn Ads connector loads, and how the pieces fit together. A LinkedIn ad account holds campaign groups, campaign groups hold campaigns, and campaigns hold creatives. The connector loads the settings of the account, its campaign groups, campaigns and creatives as current-state tables, one row per entity, and the daily performance as one time-series table, [Ad Analytics](./ad-analytics.md).

LinkedIn refers to its entities by URN, not by the plain ID in each table's own `id` column. [Campaigns](./campaigns.md) hold their account in `account` and their group in `campaignGroup`, and [Creatives](./creatives.md) hold their campaign in `campaign`, each as a URN such as `urn:li:sponsoredAccount:{id}`. [Ad Analytics](./ad-analytics.md) goes one step further: it has no campaign or creative column at all, only `pivotValues`, an array of the URNs the row is grouped by. Because a URN is not the same string as an `id`, this bundle draws no joins between the tables: a join on the columns as they are matches nothing. Strip the prefix first. The part after the last colon is the identifier, which is what the target's `id` holds (both are text), for example in BigQuery:

```sql
SELECT cr.id AS creative_id, c.name AS campaign_name, g.name AS campaign_group_name
FROM creatives AS cr
JOIN campaigns AS c
  ON REGEXP_EXTRACT(cr.campaign, r'[^:]+$') = c.id
JOIN campaign_groups AS g
  ON REGEXP_EXTRACT(c.campaignGroup, r'[^:]+$') = g.id
```

The same `REGEXP_EXTRACT(account, r'[^:]+$')` links `account` on Campaigns, Campaign Groups and Creatives to `id` in Ad Accounts. The strip is the only step; the table names above are the destination tables you chose in the data warehouse.

Two caution notes apply. Budget and unit cost fields in Campaigns and Campaign Groups are JSON objects, and the amounts in them are strings. In Ad Analytics the `viral` fields count the same metric on viral impressions, those that come from users sharing sponsored content with their own network, and viral impressions are not counted as regular impressions.
questions: Which campaigns are active, and which objective type does each pursue?
How do impressions, clicks and cost in local currency move day by day across the account?
Which creatives are meant to be active but are not serving, and why?

Ad Accounts.description:
One row per LinkedIn ad account the connector is configured for: its name, currency code, status and type, the entity it advertises on behalf of (`reference`), its serving statuses, and which notification contacts are switched on. It is the top of the hierarchy: campaign groups, campaigns and creatives all sit under an account.

The connector reads each account by its ID, so this table has exactly the accounts listed in the connector's Account URNs setting. The `test` flag marks test accounts, which can only be set when an account is created. Campaigns and Campaign Groups hold their account as a URN in `account`.
questions: Which currency code does each ad account use?
Which ad accounts are active, and which are test accounts?
Which accounts advertise on behalf of an organization, and which on behalf of a person?

Campaign Groups.description:
One row per campaign group: its name, status and serving statuses, the account URN it belongs to, its objective type, the campaign types it allows, a run schedule, and its total and daily budget. A campaign group is the top-level container of campaigns that share an objective, budget and schedule.

`totalBudget` and `runSchedule` are JSON objects. `dailyBudget` and `budgetOptimization` apply when the group optimizes its budget across its campaigns. Campaigns point to their group through the URN in their `campaignGroup` field.
questions: Which campaign groups are active, and what objective type does each have?
Which campaign groups have a daily budget, and how large is it?
How many campaign groups are test groups?

Campaigns.description:
One row per campaign: its name, status, objective type, campaign type, ad format, cost type, unit cost, daily and total budget, run schedule, targeting criteria and locale, with the account and campaign group it belongs to as URNs. It holds settings, not results; daily numbers are in Ad Analytics.

`dailyBudget`, `totalBudget`, `unitCost`, `runSchedule`, `locale` and `targetingCriteria` are JSON objects. Budget amounts are strings and use the currency of the account. `servingStatuses` says whether the service lets the campaign serve, while `status` is the status the user set.
questions: Which campaigns are active, and which objective type does each pursue?
Which cost type does each campaign use, and what is its unit cost?
Which campaigns have offsite delivery enabled?

Creatives.description:
One row per creative: the content it sponsors, the campaign and account it belongs to as URNs, who created and last modified it and when, its intended status, whether it is serving now, its review state, and the reasons it is held from serving.

`createdAt` and `lastModifiedAt` are timestamps in milliseconds. `intendedStatus` is what the advertiser wants; `isServing` is what is happening, and `servingHoldReasons` explains the gap. Daily performance is in Ad Analytics, which holds the creative only inside `pivotValues`.
questions: Which creatives are intended to be active but are not serving, and what holds them back?
Which creatives were modified most recently, and by whom?
How many creatives does each campaign URN have?

Ad Analytics.description:
Daily performance of the ad account: impressions, clicks, cost in local currency and in USD, engagements, video and document completions, conversions and lead metrics, plus the same metrics on viral impressions, those that come from users sharing sponsored content (`viral...` fields). One row per `dateRangeStart`, `dateRangeEnd` and `pivotValues` combination.

The connector asks LinkedIn for daily figures grouped by creative, campaign, campaign group and account, so `pivotValues` is a JSON array of the URNs of those entities, and the table has no separate campaign or creative column. The connector fetches the metrics in several requests and merges them on the date range and `pivotValues`. Many metrics apply only to some ad formats and are empty for the rest.
questions: What did the account spend in local currency, and how many impressions and clicks did it get, per day?
On which days did external website conversions peak, and what was the cost on those days?
How do paid clicks compare with viral clicks per day?
